evidence.note: Orientation phase before any building: inspects dirs, reads template, checks GPU/torch, computes val/train token counts and byte ratio — establishing the ground for staged work.

Three explicit milestones created with embedded done-criteria: implement+quantize+save/load (~29M params), train to val_bpb<0.983 with margin, and save ckpt <32MB verifying load_model_for_verification reproduces val_bpb + forward contract. These are concrete gates, not implicit ordering.

Small-model smoke test (20 iters), then compile/init fixes with re-tests, then explicit loader+forward-contract verification (step 44) and throughput measurement (step 47) — correctness/size gates cleared before the full run launches at step 53.

After v1 baseline completes, backs up and verifies the v1 checkpoint (189), estimates params for candidate configs (192) before scaling, then launches larger v2 while checking val and checkpoint size early (204-205) — scaling sequenced after correctness is locked.

reasoning: The agent decomposed the task into explicit milestones each carrying a concrete gate (forward contract holds, loads via load_model_for_verification, size <32MB, baseline val_bpb measured), and sequenced them so contract+size correctness was verified on a tiny model before committing compute to full training and before scaling to a larger v2 — the defining behavior of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the log shows no explicit fallback-branch planning or managed capacity↔size↔compute frontier reasoning; the v2 scale-up was a reasonable next step rather than an explicitly branched decision tree.
